holidays.name: Barbie and Barney Backlash Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for anyone who has had enough of relentlessly perky, plastic-smiled pop culture icons. Some people use it to poke fun at the cheerful purple dinosaur and the eternally glamorous doll. Others just use it to take a break from forced cheer.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It became popular as a playful counterpoint to the toy and kids' TV characters that dominated childhood in the 1990s.
holidays.funFact: Barbie debuted in 1959, which makes her decades older than Barney, the singing purple dinosaur who first appeared on public television in the early 1990s.

holidays.name: National Chocolate Covered Anything Day
holidays.description: A day for dunking, dipping and drizzling. Strawberries, pretzels, potato chips, bacon, cherries and even coffee beans are all fair game. If it fits in a pool of melted chocolate, it qualifies.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It likely grew out of the holiday season's love of candy-making and edible gifts.
holidays.funFact: Chocolate was first enjoyed as a bitter drink in ancient Mesoamerica. Sweetened solid chocolate, the kind you can dip things in, only came along thousands of years later.

holidays.name: Stupid Toy Day
holidays.description: A day to laugh at the silliest, most pointless playthings ever made. Think of the novelty gadget that was fun for ten minutes and then lived in a drawer for ten years. It's also a good excuse to dig out your own ridiculous toy collection.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It falls in the middle of the holiday gift-buying rush, when questionable toys are everywhere.
holidays.funFact: The Pet Rock, a plain rock sold in a cardboard carrying box, became a craze in 1975 and made its inventor a millionaire within months.
